concepts.def: A body remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force.
F = ma. Resultant force on a body equals mass times acceleration. Vector equation.
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Forces come in pairs on different bodies.
Mass m is amount of matter (kg). Weight W = mg (newtons). On Earth, g ≈ 9.8 N/kg.
F ≤ μR (where R = normal reaction, μ = coefficient of friction). Limiting friction reached when motion impending.
Split forces into perpendicular components (e.g., horizontal/vertical or along/perpendicular to inclined plane).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Forces & Newton's Laws — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Forces & Newton's Laws brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Forces & Newton's Laws.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 5 kg mass has resultant force 20 N. Its acceleration is:
options: 4 m/s²
100 m/s²
25 m/s²
15 m/s²

mcqs.q: On Earth, the weight of a 10 kg object (take g = 9.8) is:
Which average is best to use for the data set [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 100]?
options: The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
The mean — it always gives the most accurate average.
The median (3.5) — it isn't distorted by the outlier 100, unlike the mean.
Cats are the seventh most popular pet.

mcqs.q: Is the result of 6 / 0.5 larger or smaller than 6?
options: Larger — dividing by a number less than 1 gives a bigger result (6 / 0.5 = 12).
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
Equal to 6, because 0.5 is half and so cancels out.
Smaller, because division always makes numbers smaller.
